personas.name: Ayesha Siddiqui
personas.goal: Family documents and expiries in one encrypted vault
personas.headline: How Ayesha stopped digging through drawers
personas.summary: Ayesha runs a pharmacy and two school runs in Lahore. She finds documents on her phone between customers, reviews family profiles on the kitchen iPad, and does banks plus Zakat on the laptop — always on-device, always fictional sample data.

day.title: Morning vault
day.text: Pharmacy keys in one hand, Ayesha opens VaultCap on her iPhone — three expiries this month, including a school passport she would have found in a drawer too late.

day.title: Documents find
day.text: Between customers a phone search finds the passport scan in seconds; she texts the school office without leaving the counter or digging through WhatsApp.

day.title: Family on iPad
day.text: Kitchen iPad after school runs: husband’s profile separate, kids’ docs labeled, everything still on-device — no family Dropbox argument.

day.title: Banks glance
day.text: Laptop for a calm look at sample bank accounts before Ramadan planning; numbers illustrative, tone quiet, no tipping or advice.

day.title: Zakat summary
day.text: Same laptop shows a Zakat summary from holdings so she can email the accountant without photographing paper ledgers.

day.title: Reminders set
day.text: Phone locks with renewal reminders confirmed. Drawers stay drawers. The vault stays the vault.

personas.name: Omar Rahman
personas.goal: Multi-currency accounts and a backup before a phone change
personas.headline: How Omar backed up before swapping phones
personas.summary: Omar freelances across currencies. Phone for day balances, laptop for encrypted export, iPad when reviewing cards on the sofa.

day.title: Currency glance
day.text: Omar’s phone dashboard shows AED and GBP sample balances before the first client call — multi-currency without opening three banking apps.

day.title: Cards check
day.text: On the sofa he reviews cards on the iPad before lunch, expiry dates visible, no glovebox archaeology.

day.title: Export on laptop
day.text: Laptop writes an encrypted .vos backup to a disk he owns — new phone week, no cloud rent, no “upload everything” pitch.

day.title: Security review
day.text: Security settings on the laptop get a once-over before the swap: demo labeled, passphrase habits intact.

day.title: Phone ready
day.text: New phone restores from the backup; the sample vault opens like nothing moved. He smiles at the boring success.

personas.name: Margaret Ellis
personas.goal: Pension and insurance papers her son can help with — large text
personas.headline: How Margaret keeps pension papers readable
personas.summary: Margaret uses larger text on iPhone, reviews documents on iPad with her son, and keeps settings clear on the laptop in the study.

day.title: Large-text home
day.text: Margaret’s iPhone home uses larger text so renewals are readable without asking her son to “just read this bit.”

day.title: Documents
day.text: Documents list on the same phone holds pension letters she used to lose in the bureau — titles clear, not tiny scan thumbnails.

day.title: Son on iPad
day.text: iPad on the table while her son helps label files; he can help without taking the papers away in a plastic bag.

day.title: Reminders
day.text: Laptop reminders for home insurance sit in the study beside the kettle — dates she can actually see.

day.title: Settings check
day.text: Settings on the laptop stay honest: demo labelled, text size kept. She closes the lid feeling organised, not managed.
